name: Herod the Great and the children of Bethlehem
charge: Slaying all the male children of Bethlehem from two years old and under
summary: Mocked by the wise men who did not return to report the child, Herod was exceeding wroth and sent and slew all the children in Bethlehem and its coasts from two years old and under, according to the time he had inquired of them. Matthew hears Rachel weeping in Ramah.
offense: Innocent blood on a scale of a town, from a king's fear for his throne. The children's only crime was their age and their address.
judgment: Matthew records only that Herod died and Joseph brought the child back from Egypt. Scripture pronounces no sentence on him; secular history records a hideous death. The law's word on innocent blood stands over the case regardless.

entries.commentary: Wise men come from the east to Jerusalem to worship him. This is prophetic; it was written that kings from far off would come and bow before him.

Herod was set up as king over Judea by Rome, and he was an Edomite, not of Israel. When the messiah is born he is troubled, and all Jerusalem with him. If the messiah were coming to save all nations, there would be nothing in his birth to trouble a ruler of the nations. Herod is troubled because the coming of the messiah to Israel means judgment upon those who hold Israel down.

The chief priests and the scribes answer at once: Bethlehem of Judea, for so it is written by the prophet. They knew the scriptures concerning the messiah. The same men who could quote where he would be born were blinded when he walked among them. Knowing the book is not the same as seeing the one the book speaks of.
Herod calls the wise men privily and tells them to bring him word that he may come and worship also. He had no worship in mind; the next verses show what he intended.

The star goes before them and stands over the place where the young child was, and they fall down and worship him and open their treasures. Gold, frankincense and myrrh are the presents and gifts David prophesied of in the psalm. What was written was fulfilled exactly.
Warned of the Most High in a dream, they go home another way and do not report back to Herod.

The angel tells Joseph to take the young child and his mother and flee into Egypt, because Herod will seek the young child to destroy him. They hid in Egypt among the Egyptians. A family that did not look like the people of that land would have been no more hidden there than anywhere else.
They remain in Egypt until the death of Herod, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, Out of Egypt have I called my son.
Herod slays all the children in Bethlehem from two years old and under. This is the same pattern as Egypt, where the ruler killed the young children to stop a deliverer from rising.
The mourning in Ramah was written of beforehand by Jeremiah.

After Herod dies the family returns, but Archelaus reigns in Judea, so being warned of the Most High Joseph turns aside into Galilee and dwells in Nazareth. Nazareth had no reputation. That the messiah was raised there was itself a fulfilment of what the prophets spoke.

At the same time the Most High will be the God of all the families of Israel and they shall be His people; the people left of the sword found grace in the wilderness when He went to give Israel rest. He appeared of old saying He loved them with an everlasting love and with lovingkindness drew them; again He will build the virgin of Israel, adorned with her tabrets and going forth in the dances, planting vines on the mountains of Samaria until the watchmen on Mount Ephraim cry, Arise, let us go up to Zion unto the Lord our God. -

Sing with gladness for Jacob and shout among the chief of the nations, saying, O Lord, save thy people the remnant of Israel; He will bring them from the north country and gather them from the coasts of the earth, the blind and the lame, the woman with child, a great company returning. They shall come with weeping and supplications, and He will lead them and cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way wherein they shall not stumble, for He is a father to Israel and Ephraim is His firstborn; the straight way is keeping God's laws. Ephraim being the firstborn means Israel is the firstborn of the Most High, set higher than the kings of the earth, who are the other nations, so all of Israel shall be over all the nations; the reason Ephraim was singled out is the tribes were not the first tribe that came, but the promise is to all Israel. -

Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations, and declare it in the isles afar off: He that scattered Israel will gather him and keep him as a shepherd doth his flock, for the Lord has redeemed Jacob and ransomed him from the hand of him that was stronger than he. They shall come and sing in the height of Zion and flow together to the goodness of the Lord, for the wheat, the wine, the oil, and the young of the flock and herd, and their soul shall be as a watered garden and sorrow no more. Both young men and old shall rejoice in the dance, for He will turn their mourning into joy, comfort them, and satiate the soul of the priest with fatness, and His people shall be satisfied with His goodness. -

A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping, Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted because they were not; but the Most High tells her to refrain her voice from weeping, for her work shall be rewarded and her children shall come again from the land of the enemy to their own border. He heard Ephraim bemoaning himself, saying thou hast chastised me and I was chastised as a bullock unaccustomed to the yoke; turn thou me and I shall be turned, for after he was turned he repented and was ashamed, bearing the reproach of his youth. Is Ephraim His dear son, a pleasant child? Since He spake against him He earnestly remembers him still, His bowels are troubled for him, and He will surely have mercy; Jeremiah speaks these words of the Lord to His people.

Set up waymarks and high heaps, set thine heart toward the highway, and turn again O virgin of Israel to these thy cities; how long wilt thou go about, O backsliding daughter? The Lord has created a new thing in the earth, a woman shall compass a man; it is a new thing that women would be out front of the man and the man pretty much serving the woman, and we can see the fruition of that today. When He brings again the captivity, the Lord bless thee O habitation of justice and mountain of holiness; there shall dwell together in Judah the husbandmen, who are the prophets bringing the word of the Lord, and they that go forth with flocks, for He has satiated the weary soul and replenished the sorrowful soul.

The days come that the Most High will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and the seed of beast, so they shall have plenty. As He watched over them to pluck up, break down, and destroy, so will He watch over them to build and to plant. In those days they shall say no more that the fathers have eaten a sour grape and the children's teeth are set on edge, but every man shall die for his own iniquity; you die for your own sin, not for the sin of the next man, for that dreaded judgment comes behind iniquity.

The Most High will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah, the northern and southern kingdom, not other nations, not according to the covenant He made with their fathers when He took them out of Egypt, which they brake although He was a husband unto them. Just as a husband and wife have a covenant for their marriage, the Most High uses that analogy for the covenant we have with Him. He will put His law in their inward parts and write it in their hearts, and be their God and they His people; they shall teach no more every man his neighbor, for they shall all know Him and keep His laws from the least to the greatest, and He will forgive their iniquity and remember their sin no more.

The Lord gives the sun for a light by day and the ordinances of the moon and the stars for a light by night, and divides the sea when the waves roar; the Lord of hosts is His name. For the Most High to cast away His people, those ordinances would have to depart, the sun would have to stop shining, the moon and stars stop giving light; that is not going to happen, so He is not casting away the seed of Israel. Only a small percentage of the earth has been discovered and the heavens above cannot be measured, so He will not cast off all the seed of Israel for all that they have done; you can even see where the seas are divided from the coast, the Pacific and the Atlantic, one seed of water divided from another.

The days come that the city shall be built to the Lord from the tower of Hananeel unto the gate of the corner, and the measuring line shall go forth over the hill Gareb and compass about to Goath. The whole valley of the dead bodies and of the ashes, and all the fields unto the brook of Kidron, unto the corner of the horse gate toward the east, shall be holy unto the Lord and shall not be plucked up nor thrown down anymore forever; this goes into the Kingdom. --- Topics: [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

On the day Israel passed over Jordan into the land, they were to set up great stones, plaster them with plaster, and write upon them all the words of this law. Here is the difference between the truth and Islam and every other religion. The stone is not to be worshipped or thought to be a god; you set it up and put the laws on it so you can remember the laws.

The stones were to be set up in mount Ebal, and an altar of whole stones built there unto the Most High; no iron tool was to be lifted upon them. Burnt offerings and peace offerings were offered there, and the people were to eat and rejoice before the Most High. Thou shalt write upon the stones all the words of this law very plainly. That is what the Most High wants remembered most: not the stone itself, but the law written on it.

Moses and the priests the Levites told all Israel: this day thou art become the people of the Lord thy God; therefore obey his voice and do his commandments and statutes. Even the other nations' own books witness to it. The Martyrdom of Man says that "God made all men equal" is a fine sounding phrase but not a scientific fact, and that those who outlive hardships and sufferings which fall on all alike owe their existence to some superiority not only of body but of mind. There is no way we could have lasted this long through what we have been through if we were not the people of the Most High: thousands of years run out of the homeland, living among our enemies, put on ships and transported all over the world, and still surviving from 1492 on up here in Babylon the great.

Moses charged the people that day: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph (which is Ephraim and Manasseh), and Benjamin were to stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people. Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali were to stand upon mount Ebal to curse. Half the tribes stood on one side and half on the other, one saying one thing and the other answering.

The Levites were to speak with a loud voice unto all the men of Israel: cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Most High, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen. Every curse that follows carried that same answer from the whole congregation.
Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. Setting light by them means disrespecting your parents and not obeying them.

Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour's landmark. Every man in Israel was allotted a certain plot of land for his inheritance individually. If you moved that landmark trying to make your own land bigger, the Most High says cursed be upon you. The allotments are recorded in Joshua and in [Numbers 27](/bible/numbers/27), where the inheritance laws are given.
Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of the way. Do not mistreat those we call the disabled.

Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow. This goes back to Deuteronomy chapter 1, where the judges were charged to judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and to respect no persons in judgment.
Cursed be he that lieth with his father's wife, because he uncovereth his father's skirt. That is nasty stuff, and the curse of the whole congregation stood against it.
Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. Bestiality is the practice of Esau, and Israel was cursed for touching it.
Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother. This goes back to Leviticus chapter 18, where the nakedness laws were first given.
Cursed be he that lieth with his mother in law, and all the people shall say, Amen. Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly, and all the people shall say, Amen.
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. That is your hitman right there in verse 25: taking payment to kill the innocent puts you under the curse.

Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. At that time this encompassed everything, including the law of sacrifice. It also applies to us today, because sacrifice is alive and well; it just transformed. We still sacrifice, only it is no longer animals but our bodies. Our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High, because the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. Christ magnified the law, as Isaiah says.

If you are surety for your friend or have struck your hand with a stranger, you are snared by the words of your mouth. Deliver yourself, go humble yourself, and make sure your friend. A surety in today's terms is like co-signing for someone, vouching that they are good and guaranteeing they will be taken care of. -

Give no sleep to your eyes; deliver yourself as a roe from the hand of the hunter. Go to the ant, consider her ways and be wise; having no guide, overseer, or ruler, she provides her meat in the summer and gathers her food in the harvest. A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands, and poverty comes as one that travels and want as an armed man. This is why in the proving stage the sisters and leadership ask a brother whether he works, has his own place, and can provide for a woman and offspring. Leadership keeps a report on these men so there are no back-door marriages. -

A naughty, wicked man walks with a froward mouth, winks with his eyes, speaks with his feet, teaches with his fingers, and devises mischief continually, sowing discord. Therefore his calamity comes suddenly and he is broken without remedy.

Six things the Most High hates, seven are an abomination to Him. He cannot be all love if He hates certain things. A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood. Because He hates hands that shed innocent blood, the murderers among Esau and the nations that took us captive and shed our blood have no place ruling over us in the kingdom, yet our people keep trying to get them in. A heart that devises wicked imaginations such as sex changes, homosexuality and lesbianism; feet swift running to mischief such as gangs and gang initiation; a false witness that speaks lies; and he that sows discord among brethren through gossip and heresies. -

Keep your father's commandment and forsake not the law of your mother; bind them upon your heart and tie them about your neck. When you go it leads you, when you sleep it keeps you, and when you wake it talks with you. The commandment is a lamp and the law is light, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life, to keep you from the evil woman and the flattery of the strange woman already described.

Do not lust after her beauty in your heart, which is your mind, nor let her take you with her eyelids. By means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread, and the adulteress will hunt for the precious life. A man cannot take fire in his bosom and not be burned, nor go on hot coals and not be burned; so he that goes in to his neighbour's wife and touches her shall not be innocent. -

Men do not despise a thief who steals to satisfy his hunger, yet he must restore sevenfold. But whoever commits adultery destroys his own soul; a wound and dishonour he gets, and his reproach is not wiped away. Jealousy is the rage of a man; in the day of vengeance he will spare nothing and regard no ransom. Let a husband find out his wife has been cheating and inquire the matter, and he may well put that brother to death once he catches up to him. -

Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying,
In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.
But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appeareth in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
Saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel: for they are dead which sought the young child’s life.

lawsResolved.text: Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
Those guilty of murder are to be put to death.
Rulers are not to be a terror to good behavior, but rather to the wicked and evil doers.
It is an abomination for a civil ruler to commit wickedness, for his office is established on righteousness.
